front: Copper(II) ions with NaOH(aq) and NH₃(aq)
back: Light blue precipitate. NaOH: insoluble in excess. NH₃: soluble in excess, giving a dark blue solution.

front: Iron(II) ions with NaOH(aq) or NH₃(aq)
back: Green precipitate, insoluble in excess; turns brown near the surface on standing.

front: Iron(III) ions with NaOH(aq) or NH₃(aq)
Aluminium ions with NaOH(aq) and NH₃(aq)
back: White precipitate. NaOH: soluble in excess (colourless solution). NH₃: insoluble in excess.

front: Zinc ions with NaOH(aq) and NH₃(aq)
back: White precipitate, soluble in excess of both, giving a colourless solution.

front: Chromium(III) ions with NaOH(aq) and NH₃(aq)
back: Green precipitate. NaOH: soluble in excess. NH₃: insoluble in excess.
Warm with aqueous sodium hydroxide: ammonia is given off, turning damp red litmus paper blue.

front: How do you tell Al³⁺ from Zn²⁺?
back: Add aqueous ammonia: zinc's white precipitate dissolves in excess; aluminium's does not.

front: Calcium ions with NaOH(aq) and NH₃(aq)
back: NaOH: white precipitate, insoluble in excess. NH₃: no precipitate or a very slight white precipitate.
Li⁺ red; Na⁺ yellow; K⁺ lilac; Ca²⁺ orange-red; Ba²⁺ light green; Cu²⁺ blue-green.

front: Magnesium ions with NaOH(aq) and NH₃(aq)
back: White precipitate, insoluble in excess of both reagents.

front: How do you tell Pb²⁺ from Al³⁺?
back: Both give identical hydroxide results. Add aqueous potassium iodide: lead(II) gives a yellow precipitate of PbI₂.
